question: Does resident-first expert grouping remove the measured within-call reload tax at a net complete-request gain over the current contiguous-token WiSP execution, before admission control is built?
hypothesis: Current token grouping reloads experts several times inside prefill. Disjoint active expert groups load each initially missing expert once, but partial output sums and repeated alignment/activation/kernel calls have a cost.
role: strong known execution baseline; no novelty or admission-method claim
baseline: current WiSP LRU state and contiguous token grouping, native vLLM0.26 Triton BF16
intervention: first group contains active resident experts plus ascending missing experts to cap; remaining missing experts in ascending disjoint groups; independent expert_map has only current group mappings; native full-input partial kernels followed by addition

workload.source: existing frozen WikiText prepared/short first four documents
workload.evaluation_independence: same four calibration documents; not new holdout; each policy generates its own future tokens/routes

warmup: both arms use identical token short warmup, expert full-cohort warmup, token full-cohort warmup, then drain and switch measured execution; compare raw measurement_initial_cache including LRU

qualification: expert matched-layer reference validation; timing excluded

checks: route slot coverage exactly once, unchanged weights and no renormalization
each call loaded set equals initial missing set and no repeats for expert grouping
same-input full-weight reference across 16 layers with all-finite and numerical error values; downstream token sequences compared, no bit equality presumption
complete request counts and arrival/token/completion timeline; all repeats retained
actual expert/KV/peak CUDA allocation and own later cache/state
accounting: copy bytes count actual weight rows; extra within-call reloads separate; host_apply and CUDA load spans overlap and are not added; request wall includes Python, mapping, repeated alignment/activation/sum, and add kernels; loading/warmup/validation retained separately

interpretation.positive: use this as the execution baseline, then test remaining request-level admission/prefill tradeoff
interpretation.negative: locate reduction, activation, mapping or other execution tax; do not falsify the research problem
interpretation.invalid: duplicate/missing contributions, nonfinite results or broken request mapping stop performance claim and trigger implementation diagnosis

claim_ceiling: single-GPU artificial-cache OLMoE native eager request experiment; no production SLO, general quality, out-of-HBM deployment, or EP claim
next_if_success: one fixed-substrate controlled new-prefill injection to determine the residual old-generation/new-request tradeoff
